steps.content: [Beach, Daytime]
You finally stagger back, toolbox in a death grip and lungs burning. Ceto hasn't moved from her spot. One glance at your heaving, disheveled form is all she needs to understand.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I told you those things would wake up. A mortal body could never truly seal a breach.
I... I got what we needed, didn't I? Couldn't you... just once... say something nice? Huff...
Besides...

After only a few words, your lungs begin to congest, a coppery tang flooding your throat. The recent encounter was minor, which means your condition is far more advanced than you feared. You suck in a few ragged breaths, fighting to steady the rising panic.
It's that mortal body that's the real miracle. You might not believe it, but Herbert... he protected me back there.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I believe it. That's exactly the kind of fool he was. Always putting everyone else first.
If you're upset, just curse at the Black Tide. Or in DisCity's direction. You don't have to be... so salty about it.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I'm not upset. Stop making assumptions.
By now, her prickly demeanor is familiar. You set the toolbox down without a word.
Alright, fine. Then tell me. Where do I need to go next?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...? Why should I tell you?
So we can fix the navigation beacon.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: How many times? I don't want to work with you—
You misunderstood. I'm not talking about working with you.

options: I mean working with the former lighthouse keepers.

steps.content: This lighthouse isn't just yours. If there's even a sliver of a chance for rescue, I think they'd all want to see it shine again.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You... what is wrong with you? Are you addicted to spouting this motivational crap?
A look of pure disbelief crosses her face as she pushes herself up from the sand, her eyes scanning you with new intensity.
What? Why are you looking at me like that?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Just checking if you've taken something when I wasn't looking. How are you this amped up?
That's right, I just had a feast. Spiritual nourishment from the soldiers of the past.
Now I have even more reason to survive. To get out of here and find my friends. That thought works better than any stimulant.

And there is no more time to waste. Your body is a frayed cord, moments from snapping. Hunger, blood loss, the shackles' backlash—this relentless triad is pushing you toward a final collapse. You can no longer be sure you'll wake up tomorrow.
This, of course, is a truth you will never share with Ceto.
If you won't tell me, I'll guess. I was a pretty renowned micro-expression interrogator back in DisCity, you know.
So... North? West? East... You blinked. East it is.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Can't be bothered with you...
There's a wrecked ship on the eastern shore, right? Might be something useful there.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: That ship's fifty meters out, half-submerged in the Black Tide. The cabins are probably nesting grounds for Tide Crawlers. Are you trying to get yourself killed... Hey!
She's barely halfway through her warning when you produce a hemp rope from your gear and swiftly secure it around your waist.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: What are you doing?
The eastern shore isn't far, right? I'm going to check it out.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The hand-cranked generator's been underwater for years. It's definitely rusted through.
So there is a generator? Now I absolutely have to go. It might still work. Otherwise... why would you even mention it?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...What?
A perverse thrill shoots through you at leaving her speechless. She'd given you nothing but grief when you first arrived, but you've since decoded her "user manual"—and now you're testing its limits.
I'm going down to look. Don't worry.
Besides... what if I actually succeed?
Turning your face toward the endless Black Tide, you hide your unfocused, failing vision and call back to Ceto with a cheerfulness you don't feel:
Creating miracles is what humans do best.
